newsitem.title: UK: Hungary asset sales aim to raise $1.1 bln in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Hungary asset sales aim to raise $1.1 bln in 1997.

text.p: Hungary said on Wednesday that it hoped to raise more than a billion dollars this year in the last phase of its ambitious privatisation programme.

"This year we are expecting approximately 150 to 180 billion forints which is around $1.1 billion (to be raised through privatisation)," said Judit Csiha, the country's newly-appointed Privatisation Minister.
Csiha was in London on a three-day visit to encourage further investment in her country's growing economy and to boost support for its European Union membership application.
Csiha, in an interview with Reuters, said she met British politicians to discuss Hungary's EU ambitions -- a central foreign policy goal.
But top of the agenda were Hungary's plans to sell state assets in a range of sectors.

So far between $5.0 and $6.0 billion has been raised through the privatisation of state assets. Csiha gave few specific details about companies and the size of stakes to be offered, but she expects the process to be completed by year-end.

Hungary's privatisation and asset management agency APV has said it expects to privatise at least 270 of the 554 firms that were in its portfolio at the end of 1996. The agency's directors were due to meet on Thursday in Budapest to set plans.
"The details of the privatisation plans will have to be clarified and certain decisions still have to be made," Csiha said.

The programme is set against the background of a strong Budapest bourse, the minister said. Among the companies due to be privatised, were electricity companies, with Budapest Electricity Works as amongst the best prepared for a stock floatation this year.

Other candidates for sale include Kereskedelmi es Hitel Bank (K&H), Hungary's third largest commercial bank by assets and shares in drug company Richter. Bus-maker Ikarus and commercial vehicle maker Raba Rt might also be sold.
Csiha called on Britain to raise the level of its direct investment.
"We would welcome the participation of British manufacturers in Hungary," she said, adding the government would be setting tenders for steel manufacturing work.
During her trip, she met representatives from CSFB, Dresdner Bank Kleinwort Benson, J.P. Morgan, Natwest, Salomon Brothers and West Merchant Bank among others.
Csiha also held talks with officials from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, British Energy, PowerGen and British Aerospace.

Csiha also met British Foreign Office Minister Nicholas Bonsor and Britain's Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang. "I asked them to assist us in joining the European Union as soon as possible," she told Reuters.
She said she plans to visit Germany and the Far East in the months ahead.
